input.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
input.rationale: Governing law is Arizona, outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), so the clause fails both the preferred and the fallback position on a material term. There is also no court venue provision; instead § 19 (p0056) sends all disputes to mandatory binding arbitration under U.S. Arbitration & Mediation rules, whereas the playbook requires courts as the dispute forum. The arbitration is domestic rather than seated abroad, so this is a deviation rather than walk-away. The redline changes only the jurisdiction words and the forum: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, with Delaware, California or England and Wales courts available as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Move governing law and forum to New York law with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, in place of Arizona law and mandatory USA&M arbitration.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We changed the governing law from Arizona to New York and set exclusive venue in the state and federal courts in New York County, which is our accepted position; we can also work with Delaware, California or England and Wales courts. For consistency we replaced the mandatory arbitration forum with those same courts.

ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof, and each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.

ops.oldText: will be subject to and resolved by binding arbitration pursuant to the Arbitration Rules of U.S. Arbitration & Mediation, (www.usam.com)
ops.newText: will be subject to and resolved exclusively by the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York
